neighbours.label: a word piece inside a rare, technical or foreign word that the tokenizer splits into several pieces, mid-sentence (retro|grade, chron|ometer, tzitz|it, nit|rate); the same sentence with a plain everyday word stays low
neighbours.short: piece of a rare split-up word
neighbours.notes: Reader of bonsai1/L15/N9881- (drop 0.06). Label is unrelated to the feeder's fixed-name sense, though a few band hits are pieces of fixed compounds (' Palm' Sunday, known ' hosts'). Everyday long words (unbelievable, playground) stay near 0; an ordinary split word ('fr|inges', 0.41) also fired in probing, so 'rare' is the weak part of the label. A rare word as the first word of the text ('Komodo dragons...') was silent in the inverse-solver run. Twitch chat was quiet; all sentences are the streamer's own.
fire: The astrologer warned that Mercury retrograde begins Monday.
The ship's navigator relied on a marine chronometer.
The aquarium staff use slow acclimation for new fish.
Scott Joplin wrote many syncopated ragtime pieces.
Farmers measured the nitrate in each corn stalk.
The rabbi explained why men wear tzitzit on their clothes.
My sister finally passed the PSAT with a high score.
The archaeologist was the lead excavator at the site.
